doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Studying Buddhism with Trungpa at Naropa
summary: After her father died she turned to Buddhism and studied with Trungpa Rinpoche at Naropa with poets and jazz musicians.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: so absolutely beautiful. And he was on heroin all day long you know. You still have these glimpses of being totally in the moment and totally identified with the music and with what you do. Oh that’s a big thing, together with it comes that we are both studying Buddhism. You know we have a big monastery here. We started studying with Trungpa Rinpoche at Naropa Institute in Boulder, Colorado. And it simply had to do with — we came over here and my father died. And I’m probably one of the more lucky ones. I loved my parents. And my mother said, “Save the airplane ticket, by the time you come back” — and I freaked out. Then there was a book that Karl had bought or brought from the library or something. And so often when you need help I open it up and there was this page that said — I say it in my words — you get confronted to something deal with it. Don’t repress it. Deal with it. Cry out. Let go. So it’s always be in the moment. It comes back to you, deal with it, let it go, and then time wears it out and it will get weaker and weaker and fade out and fade out. And it helped me tremendously. And that brought me to Buddhism, you know. Because I’ve never been in any other religion than we deeply believing in Jesus Christ you know. But that part of it is the one that — Trungpa Rinpoche, that whole Naropa Institute, was full of poets, dancers and musicians. Alan Ginsberg, William Burrows, I mean all these people were there. And Dave Holland. I mean we all went out there. Lots of jazz musicians.
Called the Naropa Institute. It’s a Buddhist university.
